Hue is chosen from the hash, but applied sparingly, for a near-monochrome palette.

2027.d:
This project is an animated extension of my previous work in static generative tilings.
It explores how visual complexity can arise from the combination of simple building blocks.

This work is written in OpenGL Shading Language (GLSL) and requires a compatible GPU to function.

There are five features exposed:
- Palette: The color palette used (out of four possible).
- Palette Cycle: The color cycling method used.
- Phase Transforms: How many additional phase transformation functions are applied in addition to the core set of six.
- Blend Mode: How phase transformation are blended. Either strictly based on time or via a combination of screen coordinates and time.

The animation can be stopped and started by pressing the space key.

This is my genesis fx(hash) project.

Twitter: @jeffpalmer
Site: https://jpalmer.dev

Lay your head down, ember-warmed; drift inward with the waltz of the sky.

Process: Forged in Hydra.

🥽⚠️ WARNING: EXPERIMENTAL ⚠️ 🥽

The low resolution preview attached to this piece will not 100% reflect what you see animated on your display.

In order to create the lush smoky magma of the feedback trails within this piece, I use two .blend() operators in the Hydra code. In their live implementation, these operators correctly turn a fragmented, boiling sea of hectic, burning feedback into a much gentler, graceful flow.

Both viewport and canvas capture methods fail to capture the piece accurately due to the presence of the .blend() operators, which are essential to making this piece what it is.

What you will see displayed in the still preview of your minted variant should be considered an X-Ray of a moment from within the imagery generated by the code. It is a skeletal component of the soul that drives the feedback to its full, electric glory.

Forever limited to 100 unique editions living on the Tezos blockchain. London - December 2021.

2148.d:
Each edition has a set number of colors which bounce within the frame. Each time a color hits the canvas edge the feedback pattern changes. Feedback level is also regulated by a sine wave, oscillating between many and few feedback zones. Every 1000 frames the colors stop moving for a while, letting the feedback take over and generate a fixed pattern and a moment of calmness.

Palettes can be small (2-4 colors), medium (5-8 colors) or large (9-12 colors).
~5% chance for a monochromatic color palette.

@d0n.xyz 2021

2200.d:
Each token contains text from a uniquely-generated logography, a character set in which symbols represent entire words or concepts (unlike alphabets or syllabaries in which symbols represent spoken sounds). Each logography is related to others in the series by the set of rules determining how each logogram is drawn, but individual symbols are unlikely to repeat across tokens.

These logograms are asemic--meaningless--but one can imagine that in these logographical systems meaning may come not just from a symbol's shape, but also attributes like color, line style, and position relative to other symbols.

10% of all tokens are set to mint in babelMode (multiple sets of overlaid logograms). Other feature and rarity settings include color scheme (10% in darkMode), line vs dot vs mixed character stroke, straight vs squiggly stroke style, grid size and character complexity, and sublimated vs engraved print style.

This is an attempt to create as many different grids with simple rules:
Every position in the grid is 1 to 3 half circles or rectangles with a randomized starting angle between 0 and 270 degrees (In steps of 90 degrees).
The different blend-modes play with the shapes and the colors.

This piece was made in vanilla JS and the rendering is entirely done in CSS. Because of that it is printable in any size you need it to be.

The hand crafted color palettes are named after Tram-Stations in Zürich. Every
mint cycles through 5 out of more then 20 color sets.

Click () -> will yield a new grid and color palette. The combination of blend-modes and general styles stays the same for each buyer.

Keydown Arrow <- -> Change the grid inclination

Keydown Space -> Toggle Gaps

PS: if you are encountering small gaps between the grid items, try to change 
the size of your browser window.

2231.d:
These sigils are assembled from elementary units I called "atoms", according to a procedurally generated recipe.
Every atom type is parameterized by angles and lengths, which are generated from a base value (𝜏 for angles) and a ratio.
This ratio is generated with an exponential distribution which I tuned to confer a good balance between harmony and complexity (to keep shapes both cohesive and interesting).

Click anywhere to toggle the activation of the sigil.

Warning: Some effects depict blood

Disclaimer:
Due to the generative nature of the piece, upsetting symbols could appear in very rare occasions.
Those are unfortunately unavoidable because of the high composability of the sigil's basic shapes.
This piece is a purely mathematical and aesthetical exploration and holds no ideological message.
